rule: Post-merge decision report is opt-in and OFF by default
description: P3 coupling. The post-merge decision report is gated on the operator key `HIVEMIND_ENABLE_DECISION_REPORT`, checked by PRESENCE, and the DEFAULT (unset or empty) is OFF. The source pin sits on ONE span in `plugin/governance/decision-autonomy.md` carrying BOTH halves of that conditional: the discriminating condition (the key is unset or empty — the DEFAULT) and the whole obligation it triggers (the deferred-report scan renders no report, NEVER invokes `hivemind:decision-report`, and makes NO GitHub call of any kind). Either half alone is rewritable while the other stays green — deleting the `unset or empty — the DEFAULT` keying flips the gate to opt-out, and deleting the no-GitHub-call clause re-admits a PR-state lookup on the off path — so both live inside the pinned span. The off path's second obligation, the one that keeps the feature idempotent while disabled, is pinned as a separate entry in the same canonical file: the overlord derives the same awaiting-report set from the same predicate and `touch`es the zero-byte `.decision-report-done` marker WITHOUT checking PR state. That entry is separate because the unconditional-marker rule and the renders-nothing rule fail independently: the scan could keep rendering nothing while silently reading PR state to decide whether to mark, which would re-introduce exactly the GitHub call the gate exists to remove. Four claim-carrying spans in the agent consumer `plugin/agents/overlord.md` are pinned as separate entries, because the default rests on each: (a) the key's NAME and its operator-config CHANNEL (the `env` block of `.claude/settings.json` committed or `.claude/settings.local.json` gitignored), so renaming the key or relocating its home is loud; (b) the PRESENCE test together with its ORDERING obligation (the check happens BEFORE any `gh pr view` and before ANY GitHub call whatsoever) in one span, because a presence test that runs AFTER the lookup satisfies the letter of the gate while performing the call it forbids, and because each fragment alone is ambiguous with the sibling `HIVEMIND_SKIP_PR_WATCH` presence rule in the same file; (c) the off-path marker obligation as the agent states it (`touch`es the zero-byte `.decision-report-done` marker WITHOUT checking PR state), so the agent and the canonical file cannot drift apart on the one write the off path still performs; (d) the POINTER, in POINTER shape per rule 3 of the pin-authoring contract — the agent names the canonical `decision-autonomy.md` (Post-Merge Decision Report Trigger) section and says it is not restated here, so severing the agent site from the canonical rule is loud while honest rewording of the surrounding scan prose is not. The section name is pinned only inside that full pointer sentence, never bare, because the bare parenthetical recurs elsewhere in the same file. A fifth agent entry pins the Skills-list annotation that marks `hivemind:decision-report` OPT-IN, OFF BY DEFAULT and invoked only when the key is set, so the skill roster cannot present the report as unconditional. The repo-guidance consumer `CLAUDE.md` is pinned at the key's operator-config home, asserting that the opt-in framing survives there for contributors configuring the key. What this fixture honestly guarantees is exactly that these word sequences exist in these three named files; it claims nothing about meaning and nothing about runtime behavior. Residuals, stated plainly: (1) a presence pin proves the off-path rules are still WRITTEN DOWN, never that the overlord actually skips the GitHub call, renders nothing, or touches the marker at runtime — the ordering clause in particular is text, not an executed sequence; (2) a meaning-preserving rewrite-around is invisible — surrounding prose that re-enables the report by default, or that re-introduces a PR-state read on the off path, while leaving the pinned bytes intact stays green; (3) the pin sees only the three files it names, so a fourth surface describing the key differently is outside its reach; (4) a NEW consumer — another agent, skill, or workflow that invokes the decision report and never carries the gate at all — is an ABSENCE defect that no fixture in this directory can detect per rule 7 of the pin-authoring contract; catching it needs a structural check in `tools/policy_check.sh`, not a presence pin.

source.pattern: When `HIVEMIND_ENABLE_DECISION_REPORT` is unset or empty — the DEFAULT — the deferred-report scan renders no report, NEVER invokes `hivemind:decision-report`, and makes NO GitHub call of any kind

consumers.pattern: When the key is UNSET or EMPTY, the overlord derives the same awaiting-report set from the same predicate and, for each run in it, `touch`es the zero-byte `.decision-report-done` marker WITHOUT checking PR state
The standing operator preference `HIVEMIND_ENABLE_DECISION_REPORT`, set in the `env` block of `.claude/settings.json` (committed) or `.claude/settings.local.json` (gitignored)
is checked by PRESENCE with a simple non-empty test, and that check happens BEFORE any `gh pr view` and before ANY GitHub call whatsoever
for each awaiting-report run it `touch`es the zero-byte `.decision-report-done` marker WITHOUT checking PR state
The canonical policy is `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/governance/decision-autonomy.md` (Post-Merge Decision Report Trigger) and is not restated here.
OPT-IN, OFF BY DEFAULT: invoked only when `HIVEMIND_ENABLE_DECISION_REPORT` is set
The post-merge decision report is opt-in via `HIVEMIND_ENABLE_DECISION_REPORT`
